attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation assumes a well-defined multiplicative boundary factor B for reflected Wilson collar collapse and lacks a Yang-Mills estimate or OPE computation showing what B and N are for actual hairpin triples.
steps: Start with fixed-collar Wilson observables W_i^delta supported in positive Euclidean time. Regulated reflection positivity gives N^delta>=0 for every finite family.
Use the cutoff-removal topology only for those reflected finite matrix entries. Entrywise convergence N^delta -> N places N in the closed positive cone, so the collar-limit matrix is positive.

Let the collar trace delta down to 0. Diagonal trace continuity rules out positive additive contacts: if the additive contact matrix A is positive and A_{ii}=0 for all i, then Cauchy-Schwarz gives A_{ij}=0.
Model the remaining boundary effect as a multiplicative Hermitian factor B_{ij}; after absorbing one-body factors, the same-theory target matrix is M_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij}.
For two observables, M>=0 is just |N_{12}|<=|B_{12}| after normalization. This recovers the previous damping threshold but shows it is only a minor condition.

For three observables, positivity requires the determinant formula involving the phase-sensitive product N_{12}N_{23}overline{N_{13}}/(B_{12}B_{23}overline{B_{13}}). Thus a boundary cross-ratio phase can be a falsifier even if every two-by-two test is valid.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite matrix algebra is valid, but the analytic bridge is still conditional: we have not proved no additive contact terms for the full Wilson core, have not derived the multiplicative boundary OPE, and have not verified Schur-preimage positivity on all realized Wilson finite matrices.

assumptions: The cutoff-removal topology controls every finite reflected Wilson collar matrix entry N^delta_{ij}=S(Theta W_i^delta,W_j^delta).
For the chosen triple, diagonal trace continuity has removed additive positive contact terms; any remaining boundary effect is multiplicative, Hermitian, and has nonzero entries B_{ij}.
The Wilson observables are normalized so N_{ii}=B_{ii}=1 after absorbing valid one-body factors into the locked observable normalization.
The same finite family is used before and after the collar trace; no gauge fixing, quotient, boundary extension, or change of test algebra is allowed.
definitions: source object: normalized collar-limit OS matrices N=(N_{ij}) obtained from reflected Wilson observables W_i^delta with supports in t>delta, after taking delta down to 0 along a cutoff-removal/RG limit for which each fixed-collar quadratic form is valid.

target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M=(M_{ij}) for the same locked Wilson observables evaluated at the reflection-plane trace, with no added boundary sector, boundary counterterm, or algebra change.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by finite reflected Wilson matrices and their boundary-defect Schur preimages.

same-theory condition: every boundary factor must be removable only by locked observable renormalizations already present in the target theory, so the target matrix is M=B^{[-1]}\circ N and must be positive on the realized Wilson cone, not merely on a boundary-renormalized enlarged theory.

equations.label: collar positivity
equations.valid_when: The regulated lattice/RG construction is reflection-positive for the gauge-invariant collar observables at fixed positive distance from the reflection plane.

equations.label: closed collar limit
equations.valid_when: The cutoff-removal topology gives entrywise convergence for the finite reflected collar matrix.

equations.label: same-theory Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: The zero-collar trace creates only a multiplicative boundary factor B and all diagonal one-body renormalizations have been locked into the same observable normalization.

equations.label: normalized three-observable determinant
equations.valid_when: M is a normalized 3 by 3 Hermitian OS correlation matrix for the intended same-theory observables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a triple with |N_{ij}|<=|B_{ij}| for all pairs but det(B^{[-1]} circ N)<0; this is a falsifier showing pairwise damping tests can pass while OS positivity fails for the intended theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the abstract finite Schur-preimage obligation into the first phase-sensitive Wilson falsifier: compute B and N for three reflected hairpin/collar observables and test the determinant of B^{[-1]} circ N.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite triple of locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar observables, fixed-collar reflection positivity transfers to the intended zero-collar Schwinger functions only if the boundary-defect Schur preimage is positive. After diagonal one-body factors are absorbed, this gives an explicit three-by-three determinant test; pairwise damping inequalities are necessary but not sufficient because a boundary phase/cross-ratio can make the intended OS matrix indefinite.

assumptions: Fixed-collar reflection positivity and closed-cone transfer have already established N>=0.
Boundary effects are multiplicative after additive contacts vanish by diagonal trace continuity and positivity.
The same-theory target identifies the zero-collar observable with the Schur preimage, not with the enlarged collar-plus-boundary observable.
definitions: realized Wilson cone: the set of finite OS matrices actually obtained as collar limits of locked gauge-invariant Wilson observables in the constructed Yang-Mills theory.
boundary Schur divisor: the entrywise reciprocal kernel B^{[-1]} associated with the multiplicative boundary hairpin factor after diagonal normalization.
finite Schur-preimage positivity: the condition B^{[-1]} circ N >= 0 for every finite realized collar-limit matrix N.

equations.label: realized cone preservation
equations.valid_when: The boundary Schur divisor is positive on the realized Wilson cone for every finite locked family of size k.

equations.label: universal sufficient condition
equations.valid_when: One demands positivity on the full positive matrix cone; this is stronger than the Yang-Mills realized-cone condition and may overstate what is needed.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonpositive reciprocal B^{[-1]} is not by itself a falsifier; it becomes one only after a realized Wilson matrix N makes B^{[-1]} circ N indefinite.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates a valid sufficient universal Schur-multiplier route from the weaker but physically exact realized-cone route.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the locked Wilson realized cone is invariant under entrywise division by every boundary factor produced by collar collapse, then the closed-cone OS passage is valid for that Wilson core. Equivalently, the map N -> B^{[-1]} circ N must be positive on the realized collar matrices, not necessarily on all positive matrices.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this branch if the Wilson collar collapse cannot be modeled by a common finite boundary factor B, or if the available RG topology cannot even define the triple reflected matrix limits.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves additive-contact vanishing, derives B for a dense locked Wilson core, and verifies det(B^{[-1]} circ N)>=0 for all realized triples with a credible extension to all finite matrices.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing sharper mathematical obligations: the obstruction moved from vague boundary covariance to a concrete normalized 3 by 3 determinant that can be computed or falsified in the Wilson hairpin sector.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone step remains valid for fixed collars, but the zero-collar passage now requires finite Schur-preimage positivity, with the first nonpairwise obstruction appearing in a 3 by 3 determinant.
The algebra must include enough locked Wilson hairpin triples to test boundary cross-ratio phases; otherwise the bridge may prove positivity for too small a sector.
Entrywise convergence for pairs is insufficient; the topology must support simultaneous finite matrix convergence for triples and higher finite families of reflected Wilson collars.
A new analytic dependency: derive whether collar collapse produces a multiplicative B, prove additive contacts vanish, and compute the three-point boundary cross-ratio entering det(B^{[-1]} circ N).

falsifiers: A concrete three-hairpin Wilson family with pairwise ratios |N_{ij}/B_{ij}|<=1 but det(B^{[-1]} circ N)<0; this is the cleanest phase-sensitive falsifier of the same-theory bridge.

A nonzero additive boundary contact matrix with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal entries; this would falsify the assumed positive-contact compatibility because a positive matrix with zero diagonal cannot have such entries.
A boundary factor B with some B_{ij}=0 while the corresponding collar correlation N_{ij} is nonzero, making the intended Schur preimage undefined or divergent.
An RG compactness topology that controls fixed-collar Wilson entries but not the joint triple limit needed for the determinant test.
A proof of positivity only for the boundary-renormalized matrix N, with no valid argument that M=B^{[-1]} circ N is positive for the locked target observables.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 199 identifies the first genuinely phase-sensitive falsifier. The pairwise threshold rho_N<=|B_ij| is valid but incomplete: OS positivity for the same theory requires every finite Schur preimage B^{[-1]} circ N to be positive. For triples this becomes an explicit determinant with a boundary cross-ratio phase. The branch therefore learned that the next useful calculation is not another closed-cone restatement, but a three-hairpin Wilson boundary OPE computation or bound.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Construct an explicit symbolic three-hairpin test family: normalize B and N, parameterize the boundary cross-ratio phase phi_B=arg(B12 B23 overline{B13}), and determine whether locality or reflection symmetry forces phi_N-phi_B into the determinant-positive region. If not, use the resulting determinant inequality as the next concrete Yang-Mills falsifier target.

The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
